jenna: quick PSA — the go generator streaming sample in the README uses context.Background() and doesn't show canceling. If auth refresh happens mid-stream the generator goroutine never returns, causing leaked goroutines on long-lived apps. Repro steps below.

ashish: oh no — thanks for catching. can you paste the snippet/repro?

jenna: sure. sample shows:
```
ctx := context.Background()
resp, _ := client.Generator().Stream(ctx, req)
for resp.Next() { fmt.Println(resp.Event()) }
```
no defer cancel, and Stream spawns a goroutine that listens on ctx.Done().

sam: hmm — our library expects callers to pass ctx from request lifecycle or do ctx, cancel := context.WithCancel(ctx) and defer cancel() in examples. README should show that. Also we should handle auth refresh: if token refresh blocks, stream should return error to avoid hanging.

ashish: agree. is this causing real failures or just UX leak?

jenna: real — ran a load test with token rotation enabled on dedicated and saw goroutines grow ~1k over an hour. stack shows goroutine stuck waiting on auth refresh channel.

buildbot: CI test 'generator-stream-cancel' failed on latest run — plz triage: https://ci/reports/4578

sam: patch idea: update sampleapp to use WithCancel, add timeout example, and change Stream to select on ctx.Done() + authRefresh with non-blocking read. I'll open a PR.

ashish: also add note in CHANGELOG and a small integ test that rotates credentials mid-stream.

jenna: thanks! will validate the PR with our repro script once it's up. :thumbsup:
